title: The Serre fibre homotopy sequence including components
statement: Let $p:E\to B$ be a continuous map of k-spaces [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] with the right lifting property against $D^m\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow D^m\times[0,1]$ for every $m\geq0$, where $D^m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:\|x\|_2\leq1\}$ (and $D^0$ is a point); such a map is called a Serre fibration. For any $e\in E$, put $b=p(e)$ and $F=p^{-1}(b)$, with the k-space fibre topology. There are natural connecting maps and an exact sequence $\cdots\to\pi_{n+1}(B,b)\to\pi_n(F,e)\to\pi_n(E,e)\to\pi_n(B,b)\to\cdots\to\pi_1(B,b)\to\pi_0(F)\to\pi_0(E)\to\pi_0(B)$, with group exactness where groups occur and pointed-set exactness at the remaining terms. Homotopy groups and components have the continuous cubical definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Paths in $B$ lift after specifying their initial point in $E$, inducing bijections of fibre-component sets along paths. The loop action of $\pi_1(B,b)$ on $\pi_0(F)$ has orbit set canonically equal to the set of components of $E$ whose image is the component of $b$; the stabilizer of the component containing $e$ is the image of $\pi_1(E,e)\to\pi_1(B,b)$. A commutative map of Serre fibrations induces compatible maps of these sequences, actions and path-transport bijections. No connectedness of $B$ or nonemptiness of fibres outside the image components is assumed.

proof.text: Write $I=[0,1]$ and use $J_r\subset I^r\times I$ from [lem-coef-cubical-open-box-pair]. The disk-cylinder lifting hypothesis also gives lifting against $I^r\times\{0\}\subset I^r\times I$: the change from the centered cube $[-1,1]^r$ to $D^r$ is the radial homeomorphism $x\mapsto(\|x\|_\infty/\|x\|_2)x$ for $x\ne0$, with $0\mapsto0$, inverse $y\mapsto(\|y\|_2/\|y\|_\infty)y$, followed by the affine change of cube coordinates; for $r=0$ both domains are a point. The cited pair homeomorphism then gives lifting against $J_r\subset I^r\times I$ by precomposing the square with it, taking a disk-cylinder lift, and composing back. This prescribes the entire bottom and all side faces, not a chosen natural lifting operation.

source.place: Hovey, Lemma 2.4.13, proof, printed p. 55, the box-flattening pair homeomorphism; the radial disk/cube conversion is written explicitly here.

proof.text: We will use the following finite relative lifting consequence of Step 1. Let $A$ be a union of closed faces of $X=I^r$, including their subfaces, and suppose $H:X\times I\to B$ has a lift prescribed on $(X\times\{0\})\cup(A\times I)$. Starting with $A$, adjoin the remaining faces in increasing dimension, ending with the interior $r$-cell; on a $k$-face its already prescribed part is exactly $J_k$, so Step 1 extends the lift over that face times $I$. The extensions agree on overlaps and the finite closed-cover pasting lemma gives a continuous lift on $X\times I$. Empty $A$, $A=X$ and $r=0$ are included.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], limits in $\mathcal K$ are obtained by applying the k-space topology to topological limits. Thus $F$ is the k-ification of the ordinary topological fibre $F_{\mathrm{top}}=E\times_B\{b\}$, whose underlying set is $p^{-1}(b)$. All parameters used below are finite cubes or closed faces and their finite products. Such a parameter is a cube (or the empty set). A finite cube is Hausdorff by separating two differing coordinates. To see compactness directly, an open cover without a finite subcover would, by repeated coordinate bisection, give nested closed subcubes without finite subcovers and with side lengths tending to zero. Their coordinate intervals have a common limit point, and an open member of the cover containing that point contains a sufficiently small subcube, a contradiction. The zero-dimensional cube is a point. Thus every parameter is compact Hausdorff. If $C$ is such a parameter and $a:C\to F_{\mathrm{top}}$ is continuous, the compact-test definition of k-topology in that same cited statement says that $a^{-1}(U)$ is open for every k-open $U$; therefore $a:C\to F$ is continuous. Conversely the identity $F\to F_{\mathrm{top}}$ is continuous, since every originally open subset passes the compact tests. Hence the endpoint maps and homotopies below are continuous into the precise k-space fibre of the statement. We use the boundary-fixed cubical maps, homotopies relative to the boundary and first-coordinate concatenation of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ write a based $n$-cube in $B$ as $\alpha(u,t)$ with $u\in I^{n-1}$ and $t\in I$, and with $\alpha=b$ on its whole boundary. Step 2, with time $t$ and $A=\partial I^{n-1}$, gives a lift $a$ with $a(u,0)=e$ and $a(u,t)=e$ on $\partial I^{n-1}\times I$. Its terminal face $f(u)=a(u,1)$ lies in $F$ and has boundary $e$. Define $\delta_n[\alpha]=[f]$ for $n\geq2$, and define $\delta_1[\alpha]$ to be the path component of $a(1)$ in $F$; when $n=1$ there is no $u$ coordinate.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: Two lifts $a_0,a_1$ of the same $\alpha$ used in Step 4 have homotopic terminal faces in $F$: apply Step 2 with parameter cube $(u,s)\in I^{n-1}\times I$, time $t$, base map $\alpha(u,t)$ independent of $s$, and prescribed lifts $a_0,a_1$ on $s=0,1$, constant $e$ on the $u$-boundary and on $t=0$. These prescriptions agree on intersections. The resulting terminal face at $t=1$ is a homotopy relative to the $u$-boundary between $a_0(u,1)$ and $a_1(u,1)$; for $n=1$ it is a path in $F$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: If $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ are homotopic relative to their entire boundary, write the homotopy as $H(u,t,s)$. Apply Step 2 in time $t$ with parameter cube $(u,s)$, prescribing a chosen lift $a_0$ at $s=0$, the constant $e$ on the $u$-boundary, and $e$ at $t=0$. Since $H(u,1,s)=b$, the lifted terminal face is a based homotopy in $F$ from $a_0(u,1)$ to the terminal face of a lift of $\alpha_1$. Step 5 compares the latter with any other lift. This proves that every $\delta_n$ is well-defined, and that the constant cube maps to the base element.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: For $n\geq2$, concatenate representatives $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in the first $u$ coordinate, as in the definition of their product. Their lifts $a$ and $c$ concatenate continuously along the same coordinate because both equal $e$ at that seam; the concatenation has the prescribed bottom and sides and lifts the product cube. Its terminal face is the first-coordinate concatenation of the two terminal faces. Hence $\delta_n([\alpha][\beta])=\delta_n[\alpha]\,\delta_n[\beta]$, with the same multiplication convention in $\pi_{n-1}(F,e)$. The maps $i_*$ and $p_*$ are homomorphisms because postcomposition commutes with this concatenation.

proof.text: Exactness at $\pi_n(E,e)$, $n\geq1$: $p_*i_*$ is zero because $p$ is constant on $F$. Conversely, if a based cube $h:I^n\to E$ has $p h$ based-nullhomotopic, choose a homotopy $H(v,s)$ from $p h$ to $b$, constant on $\partial I^n$. Lift it by Step 2 with initial lift $h$ and prescribed constant lift $e$ on $\partial I^n\times I$. Its terminal map lies in $F$ and its lift is a based homotopy in $E$ from $h$ to that terminal map. Thus $\ker p_*=\operatorname{im} i_*$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: Exactness at $\pi_n(B,b)$, $n\geq1$: a representative $p h$ of an image class has lift $h$ with terminal face constant $e$, so $\delta_n p_*[h]$ is the base element. Conversely, suppose $\delta_n[\alpha]$ is the base element, and use its lift $a$ from Step 4. For $n\geq2$ take a based homotopy $k(u,s)$ in $F$ from $a(u,1)$ to $e$; for $n=1$ take a path in $F$ from the endpoint of $a$ to $e$. Concatenating $a$ and $k$ in the $t$ coordinate gives a based $n$-cube $h$ in $E$ whose projection is $\alpha$ followed by a constant segment; the formula $\alpha(u,(1-s)\min(2t,1)+st)$, $0\leq s\leq1$, is a boundary-fixed homotopy from this projection to $\alpha$. Therefore $p_*[h]=[\alpha]$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: Exactness at $\pi_n(F,e)$, $n\geq1$: the lift $a(u,t)$ defining $\delta_{n+1}[\alpha]$ is itself a based homotopy in $E$ from the constant $n$-cube to its terminal face, so $i_*\delta_{n+1}=0$. Conversely, if $f:I^n\to F$ is based-nullhomotopic in $E$, choose a based homotopy $a(u,t)$ in $E$ from $e$ to $f$. Then $\alpha=p a$ is a based $(n+1)$-cube in $B$ and $a$ is an allowed lift, so $\delta_{n+1}[\alpha]=[f]$. In particular this proves the term $\pi_2(B,b)\to\pi_1(F,e)\to\pi_1(E,e)$ that is not covered by exactness solely at $\pi_n(E)$ and $\pi_n(B)$.

proof.text: Path lifting is the original hypothesis with $m=0$. For a path $\beta:b_0\leadsto b_1$, two lifts with the same initial point have endpoints in the same fibre component: Step 2 with parameter $s\in I$, time $t$, base $\beta(t)$, prescribed two lifts at $s=0,1$ and the fixed initial point at $t=0$ gives a terminal path in the fibre over $b_1$. If the initial points are joined by a path $\lambda(s)$ in the fibre over $b_0$, lift the base homotopy $\beta(t)$ with initial lift $\lambda(s)$; its terminal path, together with the preceding independence of lifts, shows that the endpoint component depends only on the initial component. Denote the resulting map by $T_\beta$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: For a homotopy $H(t,s)$ between paths $\beta_0,\beta_1$ relative to their endpoints, Step 2 in time $t$ with parameter $s$, constant initial lift $x$, and prescribed chosen lift of $\beta_0$ at $s=0$, gives a terminal path in the fibre. Hence $T_{\beta_0}=T_{\beta_1}$. Concatenating actual lifts gives $T_{\beta*\gamma}=T_\gamma\circ T_\beta$; constant lifts give $T_{\mathrm{const}}=1$, and the retracing homotopy $R(t,s)=\beta((1-s)\min(2t,2-2t))$ contracts $\beta*\bar\beta$ relative to its endpoints. The formula $\bar R(t,s)=\beta(1-(1-s)\min(2t,2-2t))$ contracts $\bar\beta*\beta$ relative to its endpoints. These two contractions prove both inverse equations, so $T_{\bar\beta}=T_\beta^{-1}$. Thus transport is a bijection and loops define a right action $[x]\cdot[\beta]=T_\beta[x]$ of $\pi_1(B,b)$ on $\pi_0(F)$, with $\delta_1[\beta]=T_\beta[e]$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: Exactness at $\pi_0(F)$: a component in the image of $\delta_1$ is joined to $e$ in $E$ by the chosen loop lift. Conversely, if $x\in F$ is in the component of $e$ in $E$, a path $a:e\leadsto x$ projects to a loop $\beta$ at $b$, and $a$ itself is a lift proving $\delta_1[\beta]=[x]$. Exactness at $\pi_0(E)$: a point of $F$ projects to $b$; if $p(x)$ is in the component of $b$, lift a path from $p(x)$ to $b$ starting at $x$ to join $x$ to a point of $F$. These are the required pointed-set kernel/image equalities; the sequence has no terminal surjectivity assertion at $\pi_0(B)$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: The map $\pi_0(F)\to\pi_0(E)$ is constant on loop-action orbits because any loop lift is a total-space path joining its initial and terminal points. If $x,y\in F$ lie in the same component of $E$, choose a path $a:x\leadsto y$; its projection is a loop $\beta$ and its terminal point proves $T_\beta[x]=[y]$, so the two components of $F$ lie in the same orbit. Step 13 shows that every component of $E$ mapping to the component of $b$ meets $F$. This proves exactly the claimed canonical bijection from the orbit set onto those components.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: For the stabilizer, a loop in $E$ based at $e$ is a lift of its projected loop ending at $e$, so its image fixes $[e]$. Conversely, if $T_\beta[e]=[e]$, choose a lift $a:e\leadsto e_1$ of $\beta$ and a fibre path $c:e_1\leadsto e$; then $a*c$ is a based loop in $E$, and its projection is $\beta$ followed by a constant path, representing $[\beta]$. This proves $\operatorname{Stab}([e])=\operatorname{im}(\pi_1(E,e)\to\pi_1(B,b))$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Hovey Lemma 2.4.16 from cubical definitions and Lemma 2.4.13; Hovey refers the sequence proof to Spanier Theorem 7.2.10.

proof.text: Let a commutative map of fibrations be given by $f:E\to E\prime$ and $g:B\to B\prime$ with $p\prime f=g p$, and use basepoint $f(e)$. Postcomposing any chosen cube lift $a$ with $f$ yields an allowed lift of $g\alpha$; Step 5 therefore gives $f_*\delta_n=\delta_n\prime g_*$ for every $n$, including the component-valued $n=1$ map. Postcomposing a path lift yields $f_*T_\beta=T_{g\beta}f_*$, which proves transport and action compatibility; postcomposition already commutes with the inclusion and projection maps. Steps 7–10 and 13 assemble the displayed sequence with group exactness at all group terms, and Steps 11–15 give its component clauses. Every argument was based at an actual $e$ or an explicitly specified path, so disconnected bases and empty fibres in unrelated components cause no restriction.
